body.statement: There exist \(0<c_\epsilon\le C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, uniformly for \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\), \[\frac{c_\epsilon}{n}\le R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\le\frac{C_\epsilon}{n}.\]
body.justification: This is the limiting benchmark when the auxiliary sample reveals all treatment and mass information but supplies no outcomes.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 5, shows that knowing \(P_X\) alone can leave constant risk; exact knowledge of \(P_{XA}\) also reveals the propensity and changes that conclusion.
body.consumer: The benchmark determines the maximum possible return from acquiring additional treatment--covariate records.
